tokyo_asakusa_nadai_ramen_yoro.price_note: PARTIAL: the shop names its bowls in its own navigation but prints a price for only one of them, the vegan ramen at ¥1,400. The seasonal announcements on the front page carry three more dated prices, recorded below as seasonal. Everything else has an empty price rather than an invented one. Tabelog not consulted: it has served Cf-Mitigated: challenge (HTTP 403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ THE FINDING HERE IS A VEGAN RAMEN ON A 1954-STYLE ASAKUSA COUNTER, AND IT IS THE CLEANEST ILLUSTRATION IN THIS DATASET OF THE TWO DIETS COMING APART. ヴィーガンらーめん at ¥1,400 is a real, permanent, priced menu item at a traditional 和風醤油 ramen shop on Denboin-dori — which is worth knowing, because a vegan in Asakusa otherwise has very little. But a vegan ramen is not a gluten-free ramen and nothing about it moves the coeliac answer: the noodles are wheat with かん水 whatever the broth is made of, and the tare on a 醤油 bowl is soy. One diet gets a whole dish; the other gets nothing, from the same bowl. ⚠ ONE BOWL IS WORTH ASKING ABOUT ON THE OTHER AXIS: 梅しおらーめん and the しお option on the 特製 use a SALT tare rather than a soy one, which removes one of the two wheat routes. The noodle is the other and it remains, so this is a distinction that matters for understanding the kitchen rather than one that opens the door. ⚠ AND THE SEASONAL BOWLS ADD RATHER THAN SUBTRACT: the 冷やし中華 comes 特製ごまだれ付き — a sesame dressing, which in Japan is built on soy — and the 坦々つけ麺 is a sesame-and-soy dip. 伝法院通り, Asakusa.

items.note: ⚠ A PERMANENT, PRICED VEGAN BOWL AT A TRADITIONAL ASAKUSA RAMEN SHOP — rare enough to be the reason this record exists, and the most expensive bowl on the board. The shop lists it in its own menu navigation alongside the standard ramen, so it is a fixture rather than a special. ⚠ AND IT IS STILL WHEAT: a vegan broth changes the animal question and not the grain one. Ramen noodles are wheat flour and かん水, and no gluten-free noodle is offered. This is the dish that shows the two axes are independent.

As of the date on this record the Shinjuku branch is on an INDEFINITE temporary closure that began 3 August 2026, with no reopening date given; the operator directs customers to nearby branches. The full card is recorded anyway, because it is the branch’s own published menu. Prices as printed; the footer adds メニューの内容・価格は店舗により異なる場合がございます. 茶寮翠泉 is a Kyoto matcha house (本店 in Takatsuji) and the Shinjuku shop is in the 新宿住友ビル 1F by Tochomae, 11:00-20:00 (L.O. 19:30), no reservations. ⚠ THE SOBA HERE IS UNUSUALLY HONEST AND STILL NOT SAFE. The shop makes its own 自家製生蕎麦・茶蕎麦 and its English labels its combination plate «Matcha Juwari and Juwari Combination Soba» — 十割, i.e. 100% buckwheat with no wheat cut, which is rare and worth recording. It is still no for a coeliac: 打ち粉 dusting flour is wheat, the boiling water is shared, and the そばつゆ is a soy-and-dashi sauce. The 茶そば (Kyoto soba) is green-tea soba, which conventionally IS cut with wheat. ⚠ THE WARABIMOCHI IS THE INTERESTING ONE: warabimochi is bracken or sweet-potato starch, not wheat, and it is the house signature in half a dozen forms — but the shop publishes no allergen sheet and several versions are served with 三笠 (a dorayaki-style wheat pancake) or come «with sencha», so each needs asking. ⚠ AND THE 三笠 IS A HIDDEN WHEAT ON THREE DRINK LINES: 特選宇治抹茶, 京都宇治煎茶 and 玉露茎ほうじ茶 are all sold もちもちお抹茶三笠つき — a wheat cake comes with the tea by default.

tokyo_ramen_jiro_shinjuku_kabu.price_note: PARTIAL BY NATURE OF THE SUBJECT: Ramen Jiro branches do not run their own websites, and the URL carried in this dataset is ラーメン二郎 PC店Ⅲ, a Jiro-documentation site that catalogues the branches — not the shop's own page. It is recorded as partial for that reason, not because the numbers are shaky: the site publishes the Kabukicho board in Japanese and English on two separate pages and the two agree item-for-item and yen-for-yen, which is the strongest cross-check available for a shop of this kind. Address 東京都新宿区歌舞伎町2-37-5, 11:30-02:30, closed Wednesdays (the site adds 営業する日も有り — it sometimes opens anyway). ⚠ THERE IS NOTHING HERE FOR A COELIAC AND THAT IS NOT A GAP IN THE RESEARCH, IT IS THE DISH. Jiro is a wheat-noodle form: the noodles are thick 極太 wheat with かん水, the tare is soy, and the broth is pork back-fat and bone. Every bowl on the board is wheat by construction and there is no rice, no side and no non-noodle item to fall back on — the entire menu is eight noodle bowls and four toppings. ⚠ AND THE FREE CALL SYSTEM DOES NOT HELP EITHER, WHICH IS THE ONE THING WORTH KNOWING. Jiro's famous no-charge コール at the counter — ニンニク／ヤサイ／アブラ／カラメ, garlic, vegetables, back-fat, extra tare — reads like a way to customise around an ingredient, and it is not: ヤサイ is boiled beansprouts and cabbage piled on the same wheat noodles in the same bowl, and カラメ means MORE of the soy tare, i.e. more wheat. The calls change the mountain, never the base. ⚠ ONE VEGAN-ADJACENT TRAP ON THE TOPPING LIST: 生とじ卵 is a raw egg served with 魚粉, bonito powder — a fish product sitting in what looks like a plain egg topping.

tokyo_canaru_shinjuku_restaura.price_note: CANARD publishes its dinner card on its own site (menu.html, a Shift-JIS page off the shop's long-running 2009 template). ⚠ READ THESE PRICES AS A COURSE, NOT A LIST. Dinner is 4,500円 before tax for カナルディナー — one hors d'oeuvre, one main and one cheese-or-dessert chosen from the lists below — or 7,500円 before tax for the chef's おまかせグルメディナー of hors d'oeuvre, fish, palate cleanser, meat and dessert. The ＋xxx円 figures recorded against individual dishes are SUPPLEMENTS ADDED TO THE COURSE PRICE, not standalone prices, and a dish carrying no figure carries no supplement. The shop's own footer says the in-store menu takes precedence and that every price shown is before tax. Service 18:00–22:30 (last order); parties from 15 people, tel 03-3200-0706. ⚠ FRENCH BISTRO COOKING IS FLOUR-FIRST AND ALMOST NOTHING ON THIS CARD IS SAFE TO ASSUME. Poêlé fish is dusted in flour as a matter of technique, cream and wine sauces are classically roux-thickened, and a fricassée IS a flour-bound stew. Three dishes are wheat by name rather than by inference — the キッシュ and the スズキのパイ包み焼き are pastry, and the オニオングラタンスープ is gratinéed over a slice of bread — and the two tarts are pastry as well. Everything else is an ask, which at a small owner-run French room is a conversation worth having rather than a dead end. ⚠ AND THERE IS NO VEGAN ROUTE THROUGH THIS CARD AT ALL: every hors d'oeuvre is fish, meat, egg or cheese, every main is an animal, and the desserts are dairy — a plant-only diner cannot assemble a course here, and the closest thing to a vegetable starter, the ズッキーニ, is sauced in Roquefort.

tokyo_sushi_shabu_shabu_yuzuan.price_note: ゆず庵 (物語コーポレーション) publishes its whole board with BOTH the pre-tax and tax-included figure on every line; both are recorded below exactly as printed. Branch confirmed: ゆず庵 新宿西口大ガード店, 東京都新宿区西新宿7-1-1 新宿カレイドビル6F, 10:30–24:00, with wheelchair-accessible seating. The chain's own footnotes qualify all of it: 「商品の一部を記載しています」, 「仕入れ状況により内容を変更する場合がございます」 and 「店舗により商品内容および価格が異なる場合がございます」 — so this is most of the board at chain prices, not a guarantee for this branch. ⚠ THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT LINE ON THE ENTIRE MENU IS A FOOTNOTE UNDER THE NOODLES AND IT IS PRINTED TWICE: 「※当店の麺類はそばと同じ釜で茹でています」 — EVERY NOODLE IN THE SHOP IS BOILED IN THE SAME POT AS THE SOBA. That is a shared-water declaration made voluntarily by the operator, and it means the udon, the ramen noodle, the harusame and the two udon 〆 dishes all carry buckwheat contact whether or not they contain buckwheat. For a coeliac it is moot — udon and chuka men are wheat anyway — but for a buckwheat allergy, which in Japan is the more dangerous of the two, it rules out the entire noodle section including the ones that look safe. ⚠ THE CHAIN PUBLISHES A REAL ALLERGEN TABLE AND YOU CANNOT READ IT ON A SCREEN. monogatari.co.jp/allergy/brand/yuzu.php offers a 26-category allergen chart covering Japan's eight 特定原材料 — えび・かに・くるみ・小麦・そば・卵・乳・落花生 (shrimp, crab, walnut, WHEAT, BUCKWHEAT, egg, milk, peanut), last updated 2026-08-25 — but it is served only as an image-scan PDF whose text layer is empty, so it cannot be transcribed here. It IS worth opening in the shop. Note what that eight-item list does NOT include: barley and rye are outside Japan's statutory scheme entirely, so 麦味噌 and beer will never be flagged by it. ⚠ AND THE OPERATOR'S OWN CONTAMINATION NOTICE IS UNUSUALLY BLUNT, WHICH MATTERS MORE HERE THAN AT MOST RESTAURANTS: 「店舗では、アレルギー物質を含む原材料と共通の設備・調理器具で調理・盛付し、共通の食器を使用しております」 — shared equipment, shared utensils, shared tableware. THIS IS A DIY HOTPOT RESTAURANT: the guest cooks their own meat and vegetables in a shared pot at the table, so gluten from a wheat noodle, a dumpling or a tteok goes into the same broth everyone is eating from. There is no way to run a strict coeliac protocol at a shabu-shabu table where somebody else is cooking udon in it. ⚠ THE 2色鍋だし CHOICE AT 580円 IS THE ONE PLACE A REAL DECISION GETS MADE, AND FOUR OF THE FIVE BROTHS ARE OUT: すき焼きだし is soy and mirin, 牛骨旨辛 麻辣湯だし is beef bone, 鰹一番だし is bonito, and 塩レモンだし is undescribed. ゆず庵昆布だし — kombu — IS THE ONLY ONE THAT READS AS PLANT-BASED AND WHEAT-FREE ON ITS NAME, and it is the single most useful thing to know before sitting down. Two broths are chosen per pot, so a vegan would need both halves to be the kombu one, which the menu does not say is possible. ⚠ ONE MORE OPERATOR FOOTNOTE WORTH CARRYING: 「※鶏しゃぶしゃぶは形を整える加工をしています」 — the chicken shabu is a FORMED product, not a sliced cut, which is exactly the sort of item that carries binder. And an egg surcharge is in force: 「卵の価格高騰の影響により、追加の卵は別途50円（税込55円）」.

⚠ THE DECISION THAT DETERMINES EVERYTHING ELSE. The five are ゆず庵昆布だし (kombu), すき焼きだし (sukiyaki — soy and mirin, so wheat), 鰹一番だし (first-press bonito — fish), 牛骨旨辛 麻辣湯だし (beef-bone mala) and 塩レモンだし (salt-lemon, not described). THE KOMBU ONE IS THE ONLY BROTH THAT READS AS PLANT-BASED AND WHEAT-FREE FROM ITS NAME — everything else on the list fails one diet or the other. Two are chosen per pot and the menu does not say whether both halves can be the same. The chain also notes that because of egg prices an extra egg now costs 50円（税込55円）.
Meat; commercial sausage often carries wheat binder.

⚠ THE ONE ANIMAL-FREE PROTEIN ON THE WHOLE BOARD. Plain silken tofu is soy, water and a coagulant — vegan in itself. What it goes into is another matter entirely: in a shared pot with somebody else's pork and udon it is vegan only in the abstract.
Mochi is glutinous RICE, not wheat — one of the few starches here that is not wheat by construction. It still goes into whatever broth is in the pot.

⚠ THE ITEM THAT CONTAMINATES THE POT. A dumpling wrapper is wheat and it is boiled loose in the shared broth everybody is eating from — this is the clearest illustration of why a shabu-shabu table cannot be run to a coeliac protocol.

⚠ Harusame is mung-bean or potato starch and contains no wheat — and the shop states its noodles are boiled in the same pot as the soba, so it carries buckwheat contact regardless. Marked no rather than ask for that reason.
Dairy. Korean tteok is normally rice, but the commercial product often blends in wheat flour.
